line.text: A folder and a half-finished crossword sit on your coffee table. Shio tucks her feet under her cardigan.
This isn't work. It's a puzzle. There's a distinction.
I'm stuck on seven across. Four letters. 'Bitter almond, but not the nut.'
Her ears stand straight up, then curl inward, like she's caught them doing something.
That's correct. Immediately correct. Do you read poison crosswords often?
I started it because a case file had the same word in it. Now it's... a thing I do. Anyway.

choice.prompt: She holds the pen out to you.

options.text: Take the pen. Ask about the case word.

reaction.text: The word was 'bitter.' It was in the toxicology report. That's all I can say.
You didn't do the face. Most people do the face.

options.text: Say the crossword is clearly a cry for better hobbies.

reaction.text: It's a cry for entertainment that doesn't require a warrant.
A short laugh escapes her, real and startled. She covers her mouth like it slipped out.

options.text: Lean over her shoulder to look at the grid.

reaction.text: Her tail goes completely still. She doesn't move away, but her ears flatten.
That's. Close. I can read it from here, actually.

options.text: Notice her ears curl when she's pleased and say nothing.

reaction.text: You let the ear thing pass. Her shoulders drop a notch, unguarded.
Nine down. 'Exsanguination, informally.' You'll get it.

desc: She needs a second pair of eyes on a crossword that turns out to be about poisons, and is quietly pleased when you get one.
